correctness.rationale: The review reproduction starts with the ordinary binary zero-run criterion, b_0=1. At each of the 50 endpoints it scans starts in increasing order and resolves candidate equalities by exact byte comparison, so fingerprint collisions cannot alter the first match. Every (R,P) pair in the frozen table is reproduced, including the largest R=24576 at n=8192, whose last needed bit is at index 32767. A length-b witness is also a witness at every length <=b, and no length-a collision before the certified R can become a collision at any length >=a. Hence each interval [a,b] has its stated first repeat, and P agrees throughout because at the first collision two earlier matches are impossible. The intervals are consecutive, cover exactly 1..8192, and each adjacent pair of rows differs, giving maximality within that domain.
residual_risks: Correctness is only for the specified finite domain; the scale patterns in the table are not proved for larger lengths.

value.rationale: Baum–Sweet is a canonical automatic word, and the initial repeat threshold measures a different aspect of its prefixes than ordinary or Abelian factor complexity. The complete finite profile through 2^13 crosses many binary scales and resolves exact transition positions, alternating earlier-index patterns and the short exceptions. For example, the upper endpoint of a plateau can shift by one past three halves of the preceding power of two (1537 versus the unshifted 3072 at the next scale). Those exact boundaries and predecessors form a benchmark for any proposed structural or all-length formula; selected sample lengths or the leading scale alone could miss them.
residual_risks: The dyadic cutoff is useful as a finite benchmark, not an intrinsic endpoint or evidence sufficient to settle an all-length conjecture.
